messages:
maya: Hey - onboarding Zeta-XL weights. I see a registry entry but the mirror job failed. Can someone confirm where the canonical weights live?

sam: The registry record points to hf://bigmodels/zeta-xl v1 -> we mirror to s3://redwood-artifacts/zeta-xl/v1/. I pulled the manifest and the s3 objects are there but the checksum doesn't match the manifest sha256.

kevin: Two quick things to check: multipart uploads change ETag semantics, and HF sometimes provides an alternate checksum. Is the manifest checksum the full-blob sha256 or an ETag?

olivia: Good call. Our manifest expects full-blob sha256. I ran `aws s3api head-object` and got ETag: \"9f3c...-5\" which means multipart. To get the real sha256 you need to reassemble or use the original HF checksum if present.

maya: Right — manifest has `sha256:2b7f...` which matches HF model card's "sha256_checksum" field. Mirror job is computing sha256 after download and it differs. Could be truncation or object encoding.

sam: Mirror job logs show this snippet: ```rs
Downloading part 3/12
stream error: premature EOF
``` Might be partial object from snapshot copy. I retried and it completed but checksum stayed wrong.

ingest-bot: ingest-job/4821 FAILED -> reason: "object-size-mismatch"; attempted-copies: 2; origin: hf://bigmodels/zeta-xl/v1; mirror-target: s3://redwood-artifacts/zeta-xl/v1/. Logs: https://logs.internal/ingest/4821

kevin: Could be cross-account replication policy applying SSE headers or content-encoding changed (gzip). Check object metadata: `Content-Encoding`, `x-amz-server-side-encryption`, `Content-Type`. If any change, blob checksum differs.

olivia: I checked metadata: HF origin had `Content-Encoding: identity`, mirror object shows `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Mirror worker incorrectly applied compression for small parts. That explains mismatch. I'll open a small patch.

nate: On tokenizer side — noticed the tokenizer config in registry points to `tokenizer.json` but HF uses `vocab.txt` + merges for this model. Our loader currently expects a single json. We need to support both formats for on-host serving.

maya: Ok action items: (1) olivia patch mirror worker to preserve encoding and re-run job, (2) nate add loader shim that accepts `vocab.txt` + merges and outputs our canonical tokenizer bundle, (3) kevin / sam run a smoke canary against dedicated infra once mirrored.

sam: I can kick off re-mirror after olivia's patch. Also can run `sha256sum` on the reassembled blob and compare to HF `sha256_checksum`. Will ping here with results.

olivia: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/mirror/compare/issue-4821 preserving Content-Encoding and skipping recompression. Small unit test added.

kevin: I'll run the dedicated canary once the mirror is green. Suggest 100-token generation and a tokenization roundtrip check: `python -c "from redwood.tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.load('zeta-xl'); assert t.decode(t.encode('hello'))=='hello'"`

nate: I'll add the loader shim and a small CI test to `eng-ml/tokenizers` repo. Will link PR when ready.

maya: Thanks all. If mirror still fails, we may need a manual copy via `aws s3 cp --no-guess-mime-type` from a bootstrap host with HF creds. Keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
